note: The surface side of the Undermere's four gates, read by meshy_walk_export.py --gates (meshy_gates.py). Positions, sills, headings, portals and arrivals are the network design's (meshy_caves/undermere/design.json, gates[]); kit_* values are this file's own. Local kit coordinates: lx to the right of a walker facing into the cave, ly into the cave from the grille's plane, lz up from the kit's sill. Facings are degrees counter-clockwise from east.

look.note: Unlit pieces lit per vertex by the viewer's own light model (meshy_looks/final.json's moon and sky light, the village's kept lights, three's Lambert, no shadows, as apps/walk draws the lit village) plus the gate's lamp, painted in; no live light is added. COLOR_0 never shows under the ink at the village's exposure.

gates.name: The Swallow Gate
gates.sees: a dark notch in the crypt knoll's lake face under an overhanging limestone lip; two pale water lines; icicles at the lip; frost on the sill; the Company's grille and its lamp

gates.name: The Cutting Gate

face.note: the blasted face in front of the export's steep snow face (31.5 to 32.0 m east, measured), as wide as cliff:024's model (y 133.26 to 139.75, lx -3.24 to 3.25); lx of its column lines beside the slot, lz of its row lines

gates.sees: a tall slot blasted in the cutting's rock face (cliff:024) behind a timber-and-iron railway grille; hoarfrost at its edges; ice on its floor; one small lamp

gates.name: The Adit Gate
gates.district: Mill Lane and the Waterwheel Lumber Mill
gates.sees: Vane's adit: a stone-lined cutting off the outlaws' trail down a 15 degree ramp to a landing; a dry-stone headwall with a timbered opening, the Company's grille at its back and one lamp

gates.name: The Old Rising Gate
gates.kit_origin_note: the grille's line (x 194.6, y -1.75 to 2.75) stands on the ledge at the cliff's foot, 10.8 m (measured in the export blend: HM_Ground_B5_10_00 10.76 to 10.82 there), not at the design's 9.45; five stone steps climb from the pool's floor (9.41) to a landing at the grille's door, and the portal stands on that landing

portal.departure: on the landing at the grille (10.83 m), 0.2 m in front of its plane: the design's point lies at the foot of the bank (9.41), 0.7 m in front of the grille and 1.4 m below it, where the walker reached it 1.7 m short of the arch

arrival.departure: on the trestle's snow west of the hollow before the steps, at the open way out of it to the ravine: at the design's point, at the foot of the steps, the walker stood among the fallen timbers and saw them at eye height whichever way it faced; from here, facing west, it sees down the ravine and walks straight out to it on the snow, the fallen timbers behind it (2026-11-21: from (187.5, -2.0) a timber lay across the way at the chest 4 m on, and nearer the hollow a leaning timber stood before the eye)
arrival.label: At the Old Rising Gate

press.note: the trestle model's own snowy base (9.7 to 11.2 m, measured) lies over the pool's floor (9.41) where the walk's ground is; its vertices under below_z go down to a cap: under the ground the collision has there inside this box, and a bank rising slope metres a metre round it, so the steps and the landing show in a hollow with smooth sides (the earlier linear fade left stretched shards of snow beside the steps)

guard.note: the body test of the field (walk_solid_guard), at every walker centre on a grid_m grid: where the trestle reaches into the body (from_m to to_m over the feet, within radius_m of the centre; the step height and the capsule radius are the viewer's, apps/walk/src/config.ts), the nearest corner of the field rises over it if it is a stone at the shin (at most raise_m over from_m, raise_cap_m in all), else the square round that corner becomes a wall: vertical faces from under its ground to over_m over the highest ground round it (the viewer's capsule climbs a steep face of the field that is not vertical)

walk_solid.note: the bowl's floor (9.41) lies under the trestle's snow sheet (9.7 to 9.9) and its fallen timbers, and a bank about 1.1 m high closes it to the west: the walker waded through them and could not climb out. In this patch the walk's ground is the snow as pressed and what rests on it within low_m (stepped onto), its small bumps eased by at most ease_m, meeting the ravine's floor at its west side; a timber or a deck whose underside is between low_m and head_m over that ground (at the chest), a point standing ease_rise_m over its neighbourhood and every point failing the guard's body test are walls: vertical faces over_m over the ground round them (2026-11-21: the walk's level had been the top of whatever stood under 1.8 m over the snow, so the walker stood on chest-high timbers, and the steep cells meant as walls were climbed by the viewer's capsule)

gates.sees: a broad resurgence arch at the foot of the ravine headwall (cliff:020) under the broken trestle; icicles at its lip; the grille across it with a narrow iron door in its middle

terrain.note: the network design's row (design.json adit_cut.terrain_rows): ground-grid vertices inside the 2.6 m strip and the clip are lowered to the floor (min), the render ground's 0.5 m grid as it is; the collision's 1 m grid is replaced inside collision_patch_m by a patch with the cutting's floor, walls, parapets and headwall
